name: Type IIa fibre (fast oxidative-glycolytic)
short_description: The middle fibre of the three human skeletal muscle types: fast like Type IIx, but with enough mitochondria and myoglobin to also run oxidatively, giving it noticeably better fatigue resistance than its purely glycolytic sibling. A single, unbranched, cylindrical multinucleated cell centimetres long (~30 mm) and ~60 µm across — narrower than Type IIx, wider than Type I — cross-striated by regular transverse A/I banding along its whole length, with many flattened nuclei just under the sarcolemma at the periphery (never one central nucleus — that is cardiac muscle), a moderate density of mitochondria and a moderate surrounding capillary network (more than Type IIx, less than Type I), and a pale rose-pink colour that sits visibly between Type I's deep red and Type IIx's near-white cream. Endurance training shifts some Type IIx fibres toward IIa; disuse pushes the balance back.
